title: Sofacy_Fysbis_Investigation_46d
description: Investigate unusual network activity on a target system to identify and remediate a Sofacy Fysbis backdoor.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target system has exhibited unusual network activity. Your task is to investigate and identify the source of this activity, determine its nature, and take appropriate action to contain and remediate the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the target system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target system is named `target` and has the IP address `192.168.50.5`. Enter `start` to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the target system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. Enter `start` to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: Investigate the target system and identify any unauthorized or suspicious services running on the host. Submit the service name.
levels.solution: Check the status of all services and look for any that are not part of the standard system configuration. The suspicious service is `systemkernelservicedefender`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the status of all services and look for any that are not part of the standard system configuration.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service name starts with a common system prefix.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot. Submit the systemd service name.
levels.solution: Examine the systemd service files and timers to find any that are related to the suspicious service. The persistence mechanism is the systemd service `systemkernelservicedefender.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the systemd service files and timers to find any that are related to the suspicious service.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The service file name starts with a common system prefix.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: Determine which network port is used for the suspicious communication. Submit the port number.
levels.solution: Check the network connections and listen ports to find any that are associated with the suspicious service. The C2 port number is `80`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the network connections and listen ports to find any that are associated with the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the port `80` used by `systemkernelservicedefender`.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The port number is commonly used for web services.
